issues.legal_issue: A landlord’s notices constitute a sufficient demand for rent arrears when, read together and in context, they communicate the arrears and a request for payment in a way an ordinary person would understand as a demand.
material_facts: The lease required rent to be paid in advance by the fifth day of each month.
An earlier notice stated that rent for February and March was unpaid and requested immediate payment of the arrears.
A later notice identified unpaid rent for February, March and April, terminated the tenancy, and requested possession of the premises.
The tenant’s reply acknowledged specified rent arrears as of that date.
The Rent Controller ordered eviction and the Rent Control Tribunal affirmed it, but the High Court set the eviction order aside for want of a proper demand notice.
issues.conclusion: The notices, read together and in the context of the tenant’s reply, clearly demanded payment of rent; the relevant notice requirement was fulfilled, and the High Court erred in setting aside the eviction order.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 14(1)(a) of the Delhi Rent Control Act, 1958, recovery of possession for non-payment requires a landlord-tenant relationship, legally recoverable arrears on the date of demand, service of a demand notice in the manner provided by section 106 of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882, and failure to pay or tender the rent within two months of service. A notice must be read from a common-sense point of view, bearing in mind how ordinary people would understand it; a demand may be apparent from notices read together and their context. The Court approved the approach in Shri Ram Sarup v. Shri Sultan Singh and distinguished Mangoo Singh v. The Election Tribunal, Bareilly, Chimanlal v. Mishrilal, and Mangat Ram v. Sardar Meharban Singh.

rule.if: rent_eviction_appeal and related_notices_read_together and arrears_identified and payment_requested and nonpayment_consequence_indicated

predicates.rent_eviction_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal concerning an eviction claim based on a tenant’s failure to pay rent.
predicates.related_notices_read_together: The landlord’s related communications are considered together and in their surrounding context.
predicates.arrears_identified: The communications tell the tenant that rent is in arrears.
predicates.payment_requested: The communications request that the tenant pay the arrears.
predicates.nonpayment_consequence_indicated: The communications indicate that a consequence, such as eviction proceedings, may follow if the arrears are not paid.

issues.definition: When a rent-eviction appeal concerns related communications that, read together, identify arrears, request payment, and indicate a consequence for nonpayment, the demand-notice requirement is satisfied.
